item.title: 1. Why Spiking Neural Networks Matters
item.description: 1. Why Spiking Neural Networks Matters This teaching step is conceptually distinct and could not be merged without blurring two different ideas.

item.title: 1.1 Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist
item.description: Why Spiking Neural Networks Exist Once a neural model has inputs, weighted connections, and outputs, it can transform raw data into useful decisions.

item.title: 2. From Discrete Spike Events to Sparse Activity
2.1 Spikes, Sparsity, and Event-Driven Computation
item.description: Spikes, Sparsity, and Event-Driven Computation Once neural communication is understood as information passing from one neuron to another, a practical question appears: when should a neuron send a message? Imagine a sensor watching a quiet doorway.

item.title: 2.2 Spike Timing and Temporal Information
item.description: Spike Timing and Temporal Information A discrete spike event marks that a neuron became active at a particular moment, and asynchronous processing allows that event to move through a network when it occurs.

item.title: 2.3 The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron
item.description: The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron A stream of spike events becomes useful only when a neuron can combine those events into a decision.

item.title: 2.4 Encoding Inputs as Spike Trains
item.description: Encoding Inputs as Spike Trains A spike train already gives us a way to describe activity across simulation timesteps: a neuron either emits a spike at a particular time or remains silent.
